subject.title: TUI /sessions list: gateway-injected inbound metadata block used as session title (shows 'untrusted metadata' for all sessions)

question: Should maintainers adopt or replace the stale conflicting fork PR before allowing a new same-repo fix for this issue?
rationale: The bug is narrow and source-proven, but an open fork PR already uses closing syntax and the issue has `clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr`, so automation should not create another fix path until maintainers choose how to handle that branch.

options.title: Replace with a narrow same-repo fix
options.body: Open or adopt a maintainer-controlled PR that strips inbound metadata in the shared gateway title reader and passes resolved title fields, then close the stale fork PR after replacement exists.

options.title: Ask the fork author to refresh proof
options.body: Keep the fork PR as the candidate only if the author rebases it against current main, resolves conflicts, and supplies real behavior proof for the TUI/session-list path.

options.title: Pause until broader title work lands
options.body: Let broader session-title product work continue, but this leaves the concrete metadata-title bug open until a specific fix lands.

recommendation.title: Replace with a narrow same-repo fix
recommendation.body: Open or adopt a maintainer-controlled PR that strips inbound metadata in the shared gateway title reader and passes resolved title fields, then close the stale fork PR after replacement exists.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent gateway session-utils history makes this the best available routing owner for choosing the repair path.
